in cod. Vindob. theol. gr. 244 [nostro 14], s. XV, idem tractatus invenitur. —
Christianos sanctos, qui in fine cuiusque paragraphi nominantur, ideo invocari nos
monuit Franciscus Boll, quia eos stellis quibusdam praesidere credebant Byzan-
tini; quod ex excerpto in Catal. Veneti p. 214 edito manifestum fit. Veterum
deorum locum illi sancti obtinere videntur (cf. infra p. 165, 14), etsi paulo aliter sen-
tiat scriptor anonymus de Mardaitis, cuius opusculum excerpto supra memorato in
codice Veneto 5 (f. 420) iungitur. Εὐσεβέστεροι γάρ, inquit, χάριν σεβάσματος τὰς
τῶν ἀστέρων τροπὰς ἁγίων ὀνόμασι Χριστιανοὶ προσανέθεντο, Ἑλλήνων ταύτας
πρότερον εἰς ζῷά τινα, κριοὺς καὶ ταύρους καὶ καρκίνους κακῶς ἐπικαλεσάντων
(cf. Morelli, D. Marci Bibliotheca, 1802, p. 218). [F. C.]
sections.en:
in cod. Vindob. theol. gr. 244 [our 14], s. XV, the same tractate is found. —
Franciscus Boll advised us that the holy Christians, who are named at the end of each paragraph, are invoked for this reason,
because the Byzantines believed that they presided over certain stars;
which becomes manifest from the excerpt edited in Catal. Veneti p. 214. Those saints
seem to hold the place of the ancient gods (cf. below p. 165, 14), although the anonymous writer
concerning the Mardaites may feel a little differently, whose opuscule is joined to the above-mentioned excerpt in
codex Venetus 5 (f. 420). For the more pious Christians, he says, for the sake of reverence
assigned the turnings of the stars to the names of saints, the Greeks having previously
badly called these after certain animals, rams and bulls and crabs
(cf. Morelli, D. Marci Bibliotheca, 1802, p. 218). [F. C.]

summary.headline: Aries Birth Predictions
summary.text: Astrological descriptions of a man and a girl born under Aries, covering appearance, character, wealth, dangers, illnesses, lifespan, remedies involving a ram’s horn and Saint Stephen, and the girl’s marriages and misfortunes. A scholarly note discusses Byzantine beliefs that Christian saints presided over stars and replaced ancient zodiacal deities.
